reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis is scientifically sound: increased grain boundary density from severe plastic deformation is well-known to enhance Cr diffusivity and promote faster, more uniform passivation in high-Cr steels, though the predicted 30-50% reduction in corrosion rate may be optimistic and depends on avoiding detrimental secondary phases.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and feasible, with well-defined measurements (electrochemistry, weight loss, XPS, microscopy) and a specific, quantitative falsification criterion (≥30% reduction in corrosion current density and weight loss, plus confirmed Cr enrichment).
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is highly useful for researchers in this field, as it proposes a mechanistic, testable link between microstructure and corrosion resistance that addresses a key challenge in chemical-processing and nuclear-power steels, with clear boundaries and uncertainties.
